prompt: A workload receives Forbidden when reading a ConfigMap. Diagnose the exact security gate and repair least privilege.
directAnswer: Bind server/context, service-account UID, token audience/expiry, audit ID and exact action tuple: get, core API group, configmaps, namespace and name. Forbidden proves authentication established identity but authorization denied. Use an approved reviewer to test the tuple, inspect Role/ClusterRole and RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding subjects/roleRefs/rules, including groups and aggregation. Grant only the required namespaced verb/resource and resourceName where practical. Do not grant cluster-admin. Verify required read succeeds, Secret and cross-namespace reads remain denied, application works and old/broad binding is absent.
foundation: Authorization evaluates one identity/action/scope tuple after authentication.
seniorAnswer: I avoid credential exposure and broad grants. I identify the exact tuple and grant path, make the smallest namespace-scoped change, and prove both needed success and continued denial outside the contract.
whyWeak: It converts one missing read into unrestricted cluster compromise potential.

evidence.proves: identity exists and exact action denied

followUps.answer: Forbidden includes an authenticated identity; Unauthorized is the authentication branch.
A creator may mount service accounts/secrets or request powerful runtime settings.
The old tuple returns denied after caches/token considerations, with audit evidence.
